title: Replacement Property Identification
name: Replacement Property Identification
metaTitle: Replacement Property Identification Support in Oklahoma City, OK
metaDescription: We build your Oklahoma City 1031 identification list from properties already walked and vetted, delivered correctly to your intermediary before day 45.

sections.html: Your identification list is a legal document with a hard deadline, not a shopping list you can quietly revise later. We build that list with you against the actual Oklahoma City inventory available in your basis range, so what you submit on day forty-five is a set of properties you've already had walked and vetted, not addresses pulled together the night before the deadline arrives.

sections.heading: What Actually Has to Be on the List
sections.html:
An identification needs an unambiguous description of the property, typically a street address or legal description, delivered in writing to your qualified intermediary or another party involved in the exchange. You don't need a signed purchase agreement to identify a property, but you do need enough specificity that there's no question which building you mean, and we draft that language ourselves rather than leaving it to a last-minute email.

Timing matters too: the notice has to be delivered and received before midnight on day forty-five, and a verbal or informal identification simply doesn't count under the rule.

sections.heading: What We Track While Building Your List
sections.html:
Before we finalize candidates for your identification, we check the details that determine whether a property actually stays viable through closing:

  • Purchase price against your basis and reinvestment target
  • Property type mix if you're diversifying across two or three assets
  • Physical condition and any items needing disclosure before you commit
  • Financing feasibility within your 180-day closing window
  • Backup candidates in case a primary target falls out of contract
  • Timeline coordination with your qualified intermediary's notice requirements

We revisit this list as new information comes in during sourcing, since a candidate that looked strong in week one can shift once we've seen the lease file or the mechanical condition.

sections.heading: Three-Property, 200%, or 95%: Picking the Right Approach for Your Deal
sections.html: Most Oklahoma City investors we work with use the three-property rule for a straightforward single-replacement deal, since it doesn't cap total value. For clients diversifying basis across several smaller assets, the 200% or 95% rules give more room, but each comes with its own tradeoffs that we walk through before you lock a list. Confirm the specific mechanics and consequences of each rule with your qualified intermediary alongside your own review of the properties themselves.

sections.heading: Backup Candidates: Why We Always Build More Than You Need
sections.html:
Properties fall out of contract for reasons that have nothing to do with your diligence, from financing timelines to a title issue on an older plat. Older Oklahoma City retail centers and apartment communities in particular sometimes carry survey or easement questions that take time to clear, so we always build backup candidates into your list rather than betting the exchange on a single address.

We treat a backup candidate as a real option, not a placeholder, which means it still gets a walkthrough and a basic financial check even if you never end up closing on it.

sections.heading: Coordinating the List With Your Intermediary's Delivery Requirements
sections.html:
Identification has to be delivered in writing, before midnight on day forty-five, to your qualified intermediary or another eligible party named in your exchange agreement. A verbal identification, or one delivered even a day late, doesn't count, so we coordinate delivery with your intermediary directly and keep a dated copy for your file in case the timing is ever questioned.

We treat that delivery step the same way you'd treat a required inspection sign-off: it either happened on time and on paper, or it didn't happen at all, and there's no version of close enough that satisfies the rule.

faqs.q: Do I need a signed purchase agreement to identify a property?
faqs.a: No, identification only requires an unambiguous written description of the property, not a signed contract. That said, having a property under contract or close to it generally reflects a stronger, more realistic candidate, and we favor those when building your primary slot.

faqs.q: How many properties can I put on my identification list?
faqs.a: Under the three-property rule you can identify up to three properties regardless of value. If you're using the 200% or 95% rules instead, the number can be higher but comes with different value constraints, which we walk through based on your specific deal and reinvestment target before you commit to either approach.

faqs.q: What happens if every property on my list falls out of contract?
faqs.a: If none of your identified properties close within your 180-day exchange period, the exchange generally fails and the transaction is treated as a taxable sale. That's exactly why we build backup candidates into every list rather than relying on one address making it to closing, and why we push back on lists that lean too heavily on a single strong candidate.

faqs.q: Can I identify a property in another state alongside an Oklahoma City property?
faqs.a: Yes, identification isn't limited by state, so an out-of-state property can sit alongside an Oklahoma City candidate on the same list. Confirm any state-specific tax reporting implications with your own tax advisor before you finalize that split, since filing requirements can vary meaningfully between states.

faqs.q: Does identifying a property obligate me to buy it?
faqs.a: No, identification is a notice requirement, not a purchase commitment. You can walk away from an identified property during diligence and move to a backup candidate instead, as long as you still have time inside your exchange period, which is one more reason a well-built list matters more than the primary target alone.
